# A rejected state-provider store replacement leaves consumers holding a destroyed store

## Context

Multiple planning panes can borrow the same store from a workspace provider. The provider owns a store it constructs from a descriptor; replacing the store is also a lifetime change for every borrower.

## The Problem

This public-API fixture was run in the Engine unit setup. The original store contained one record and was shared by a root and a child provider.

```js
const root = Neo.create(Provider, {stores: {
    plan: {module: Store, keyProperty: 'id', data: [{id: 'task'}]}
}});
const child = Neo.create(Provider, {parent: root});
const original = child.getStore('plan');
root.stores = {plan: {module: Store, keyProperty: 'id'}, invalid: null};
```

The setter throws while reading the invalid entry's listeners. After the rejection, `child.getStore('plan') === original` and `original.isDestroyed === true`. The branch used for the probe has identical `Neo.mjs`, `core/Base.mjs` and `state/Provider.mjs` to `dev` at `0cc7e43087`.

## The Architectural Reality

[`Provider#beforeSetStores`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/0cc7e43087/src/state/Provider.mjs#L283) destroys unretained owned stores before constructing the successor descriptor map. The reactive setter can reject before publishing a new map. A hierarchy lookup still resolves the old map, while the old store's teardown has already happened. Explicit-ID replacement also relies on releasing an ID before reusing it.

## The Fix

Make replacement failure coherent for borrowers. Preserve the existing successful replacement, explicit-ID reuse, sibling source references and teardown of provider-owned stores. Verify temporary successors are retired on a failure partway through a multi-key replacement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A rejected replacement leaves the original store, its record data and its registration usable through the child provider. Include the malformed later descriptor and a later store constructor that rejects an otherwise well-formed config.
- [ ] No failed successor remains registered or becomes the store resolved by a borrower. A corrected retry succeeds.
- [ ] Existing explicit-ID reuse, implicit generations and borrowed-store survival controls remain green.

## Out of Scope

Changes to every reactive setter or a release-wide ban on store replacement.

## Related

Shared-plan consumer #21915. Live latest-open + closed sweep: newest 24 Engine issues and all-state provider/store replacement, beforeSetStores and owned-store searches. Existing ownership fixes and Provider's replacement specs cover successful transitions. This fixture exercises a rejected transition.
